lessons: - [any] When picks fall short or fail, search more brand pages for a dated, sourced replacement; never leave a post unstarted.
- [MARKET] Match each number to its named source, dropping unsupported figures; say "leads" or "largest" only when verified.
- [MARKET] Count the cover headline's words against the six-word maximum before rendering; shorten until it fits.
- [MARKET] Give each slide a new fact, never repeat an earlier figure; date any figure older than a few weeks.
- [MARKET] Keep table rows to one line by shortening labels and values; show bare numbers when the label names the measure.
- [LISTICLE] Take prices only from the brand or an official retailer dated this month; drop aggregators such as WatchCharts.
- [LISTICLE] Before rendering, add picks until slides fit the format's range; re-derive folder name, cover number and caption from the final list.
- [LISTICLE] Check queue/approved and recent posts; replace any watch already featured there with a new model.
- [LISTICLE] Confirm each pick's photo is rights-cleared in permissions.json or the asset manifest and shows the named reference; otherwise swap it.
- [LISTICLE] Visually review every rendered slide before finishing; fix any photo, model or text mismatch.
- [LISTICLE] Before finishing, fill every research handoff field and rerun validate until it passes.
- [WOULD YOU RATHER] Keep product names to two lines in side-by-side columns; keep footnotes legible with clear space above the footer.
